motions.motion_text: Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Osborne to approve consent items 3A through 3J with item 3H pulled from consent by Deputy Mayor Gray.

Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Wilson to adopt Ordinance No. 7694 adopting the 2010 budget; adopt Ordinance No. 7695 establishing the property tax mill levy for 2009 to be collected in 2010; adopt Ordinance No. 7696 appropriating the 2010 budget; adopt Ordinance No. 7697 changing certain fees; adopt Ordinance No. 7698, as amended, changing certain development excise taxes, the education excise tax and impact fees.

Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Morzel to amend the main motion to direct the City Manager to institute a budget reallocation to keep the Meadows and George Reynolds Branch Library as they currently are in 2009 for 2010 (option A3).
Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Cowles to amend the main motion to direct the City Manager to restore the main library hours on Sundays.

Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Morzel to amend the main motion to direct the City Manager to return with options for a phased spending plan to fund the Community Literacy Program in 2010 depending on revenue targets and spending priorities.
motions.vote_text: The motion failed 4:4; Appelbaum, Ageton, Espinoza, and Osborne opposed.

motions.motion_text: Vote was taken on the main motion to adopt Ordinance No. 7694 adopting the 2010 budget; adopt Ordinance No. 7695 establishing the property tax mill levy for 2009 to be collected in 2010; adopt Ordinance No. 7696 appropriating the 2010 budget; adopt Ordinance No. 7697 changing certain fees; adopt Ordinance No. 7698, as amended, changing certain development excise taxes , the education excise tax and impact fees.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried unanimously 8:0 with Espinoza opposed to Ordinance No. 7698.

motions.motion_text: Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Appelbaum to adopt Resolution No. 232 adopting the 2010 budget for the Downtown Commercial District Fund; adopt Resolution No. 233 establishing the 2009 property tax mill levy for the Central Area General Improvement District; and adopt Resolution No. 234 appropriating money to defray the expenses and liabilities of the Downtown Commercial District Fund for the 2010 fiscal year.

Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Appelbaum to adopt Resolution No. 171 adopting the 2010 budget for the University Hill Commercial District Fund; adopt Resolution No. 172 establishing the 2009 property tax mill levies for the University Hill General Improvement District; and adopt Resolution No. 172 appropriating money to defray the expenses and liabilities of the University Hill Commercial District Fund for the 2010 fiscal year.
Council Member Ageton moved, seconded by Appelbaum to adopt Resolution No. 130 adopting the 2010 budget for the Boulder Municipal Property Authority.

Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Appelbaum to adopt Resolution No. 31 adopting the 2010 budget for the Forest Glen Transit Pass General Improvement District; adopt Resolution No. 32 establishing the 2009 property tax mill levies for the Forest Glen Transit Pass General Improvement District for the 2010 fiscal year; and adopt Resolution No. 33 appropriating money to defray the expenses and liabilities of the Forest Glen Transit Pass General Improvement District for the 2010 fiscal year.

Council Member Osborne moved, seconded by Morzel to adopt Ordinance No. 7692 designating the building and site at 1143 13th Street, to be known as the Silver & Gold Cleaners/Payne's Shoe Shop; and Ordinance No. 7693 designating the building and site at 1155 13th Street, to be known as the Kinsely & Co. Building.

Council Member Wilson moved, seconded by Espinoza to adopt Ordinance No. 7690 amending Section 4-20-46, “Stormwater and Flood Management Utility Plant Investment Fee,” B.R.C. 1981, and setting forth related details.
motions.vote_text: This item was continued to later in the meeting.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Cowles to introduce and order published by title only Ordinance No. 7701 amending the land use code (Title 9, B.R.C) to repeal Chapter 9-13 B.R.C. Inclusionary Zoning and adopt the proposed Chapter 9-13 B.R.C. Inclusionary Housing to be effective 60 days after final reading or March 1, 2010, whichever is later, in order to incorporate changes recommended by City Council in conjunction with Phase II of the Affordable Housing Review.
Mayor Appelbaum moved, seconded by Morzel to suspend the rules and continue the meeting at 10:45 p.m.

Council Member Wilson moved, seconded by Espinoza to adopt Ordinance No. 7690 amending Section 4-20-46, “Stormwater and Flood Management Utility Plant Investment Fee,” B.R.C. 1981, and setting forth related details.

Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Wilson to adopt Ordinance No. 7691 to implement an intergovernmental agreement with the Town of Nederland regarding improvements to Nederland’s wastewater treatment facility at Barker Reservoir in the form of Exhibit A of Attachment A of the agenda memo and to authorize the City Manager to approve any non-substantive changes that might be made subsequent to City Council’s approval.
Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Gray to reject the Junior Academy area plan.

agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council adopted Ordinances 7694, 7695, 7696, 7697, and 7698, with amendments to library hours and a phased spending plan for the Community Literacy Program.

agenda_items.title: CONSIDERATION OF THREE RESOLUTIONS PERTAINING TO THE 2010 BUDGET OF THE CITY OF BOULDER DOWNTOWN COMMERCIAL DISTRICT FUND (FORMERLY KNOWN AS THE CENTRAL AREA GENERAL IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT FUND).

INCLUSIONARY ZONING AND ADOPT THE PROPOSED CHAPTER 9-13 B.R.C. agenda_items.outcome_summary: Council introduced and ordered published by title only Ordinance 7701 to repeal Chapter 9-13 B.R.C. Inclusionary Zoning and adopt the proposed Chapter 9-13 B.R.C. Inclusionary Housing.
